methodology.description: Tests the 'Rhetorical Pivot / Are Moderate Voters Rubes?' hypothesis and decomposes Economic Moderation vs. Cultural/Identity Moderation as independent variables across 49 major 2026 U.S. Senate, Gubernatorial, Attorney General, and competitive/PAC-targeted U.S. House candidates. Separates (1) Objective Past Record & Institutional Alignment (Voteview DW-NOMINATE roll-call votes, House caucus membership, pre-2026 M4A/GND/ICE positions, and FEC Independent Expenditures by progressive vs. moderate PACs) from (2) Blinded 2026 General-Election Rhetoric & Media Appearances (scraped pre-election news, TV/podcast/debate interviews, YouTube appearances, and Bluesky posts with candidate names and states redacted as [CANDIDATE] and [STATE] before scoring via opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free).
methodology.key_finding: Both Economic Moderation (+2.81 pts/unit statewide, p=0.0007) and Cultural/Identity Moderation (+3.47 pts/unit, p=0.0003) independently boost 2026 overperformance (joint R2 = 0.294). Anti-billionaire economic populism alone has zero bivariate effect (r = -0.07, p=0.69), but interacting economic populism with a moderate economic & cultural record pushes statewide R2 to 0.450 (+5.48 pts, p=0.011): Cross-Partisan Economic Populists (+4.72 pts statewide, 10-for-11) and Pro-Business Moderates (+3.14 pts all, 77.3% beat House) both win, whereas candidates with hard-left economic records who ran on cultural moderation or anti-billionaire populism (Troy Jackson -8.78, Deb Haaland -7.97, Gina Hinojosa -1.32) went 0-for-5 statewide (-4.10 pts).
